title: Mercurius — A Zero-Trust Network‑Native Window System
excerpt: Use your real workstation securely from anywhere. Mercurius is a clean, modern window system designed for remote presence, strong security, and powerful machines.
content_html:
Graphical sessions you can put down and pick up again.

Pick up your work exactly where life made you stop, whether on the same machine or from elsewhere.

Mercurius gives you long‑lived graphical sessions that you can leave, return to, and resume whether you’re on the same laptop or somewhere else on the network. The session model works locally without any networking at all; the network simply lets your sessions inhabit more powerful machines when you want them to.

In a nutshell, Mercurius does for the GUI what ssh does for the CLI.

Sometimes life interrupts. You're busy when work calls, the kids want you, dinner is ready, or you need to do something else for a while. Mercurius treats sessions as first-class objects so your applications belong to the session, not the physical device in front of you.

It used to be normal to share the big, expensive computer in the corner but today everyone has a laptop so that is out of fashion. Meanwhile the economics of computing have changed again: RAM and GPUs are costly, and workstation‑class machines deliver far more capability than most people carry around. Mercurius lets you use that capability without giving up the convenience of your own environment. You keep your work on your own machines, so you’re never at the mercy of a cloud subscription just to read your own documents. Sharing the expensive computer again makes sense. Mercurius lets an organisation concentrate its investment in a few powerful GPU‑rich workstations and make full use of them, instead of buying every developer a high‑end laptop that can’t run the heavy workloads anyway.
